layout_thesis.statement: The whole brand fits in three words — just add spirit — so the page is built as a ratio, not a brochure. A warm cream field runs top to bottom like a Charleston kitchen counter; the seven bottles are the constant object on it, and the finished drinks are the payoff. Every section answers one question a drinker actually has, in order: what is it, what's the ratio, what's in it, who made it, what can I make, and where do I buy it. Nothing is explained twice.
layout_thesis.audience: Home drinkers who want a good cocktail in under a minute and read ingredient labels, plus the bar and shop buyers who stock them.
layout_thesis.job_to_be_done: Convince someone in one scroll that a $12 bottle replaces a shelf of ingredients, then get them to the shop.
layout_thesis.why_this_not_generic: A generic DTC beverage page opens on a lifestyle photo and buries the product behind a mood. This one opens on the rule (2:1) because that is the brand's actual promise and its shortest sentence. The bottles are treated as a repeated typographic object rather than a carousel, and the recipe library is presented as an index of spirits rather than a grid of cards — because the brief says recipes are the SEO engine and are tagged by spirit, not by mood.

signature_element.name: The ratio mark
signature_element.description: The figure 2:1 set in the display face at headline scale, used once as a full section and then echoed at small size beside the Bloody Mary's 4:1 exception. The colon is set in the teal accent; the numerals in the brown text colour.
signature_element.why_it_fits_brand: The mix ratio is the single most repeated fact on the live site and the entire product promise — two parts mixer, one part spirit. It is a number the brand already owns, so it needs no explanation and cannot be mistaken for another beverage brand.
signature_element.implementation_note: Rendered as text in the display family, not an image, so it inherits the type scale and stays crisp at any viewport. The teal is the brief's single saturated accent (#259E7E) and appears nowhere else on the page except links.

effects: short fade-and-rise on section entry, under 200ms
no parallax, no scroll-jacking, no autoplaying carousels
motion_vocabulary.rationale: The brand voice is plain and unhurried — short sentences, no showmanship. Motion that draws attention to itself would contradict 'real people, real ingredients'. Entry fades only, so the page reads at reading speed.

sections.purpose: Site header carrying the wordmark and the brand's one-line origin.
sections.component: masthead strip; wordmark left, tagline beside it, section nav right
sections.rationale: The live site's logo IS its typography — there is no logo asset — so the wordmark is set in the display face rather than an image.

sections.purpose: Open on the product promise: seven mixers, one ratio, no bar skills required.
sections.component: split hero; oversized headline left, the Classic Margarita bottle standing right
sections.rationale: Leads with the ratio because it is the brand's shortest and most repeated claim, and because it answers the only real objection — that mixing a cocktail at home is fussy.

media.alt: Classic Margarita 1L bottle on its drop shadow
media.rationale: The bottle is the constant object of the brand; showing it first makes the product, not a mood, the opening image.

sections.purpose: State the mix ratio as the signature element.
sections.component: pull quote; the ratio mark at display scale with the exception noted beneath
sections.rationale: Given a whole section rather than a footnote because it is the signature element and the fastest thing to remember.

sections.purpose: Back the 'real' claim with what is and is not in the bottle.
sections.component: full-bleed ingredient flat-lay with the claim above it
sections.rationale: The word 'real' is the brand's core repetition, so it gets the page's only edge-to-edge image — the claim is shown before it is argued.

media.alt: Flat-lay of the real ingredients used in the mixers — citrus, cucumber, chiles and sea salt
media.rationale: A photograph of the actual ingredients is the only honest way to support an ingredients claim.

sections.purpose: Name all seven mixers so a visitor can find theirs.
sections.component: card grid; one card per mixer, numbered
sections.rationale: A grid rather than a carousel: all seven are the product range, and hiding four behind a swipe would bury the thing being sold.

sections.purpose: Say who makes it and where, with the founders shown.
sections.component: feature split; founders photograph one side, origin copy the other
sections.rationale: 'Made by real people' is a claim that needs faces. The founders' own photograph does the work a paragraph cannot.

media.alt: Joe and MariElena Raya, the founders of Barcoop Bevy
media.rationale: The brief's only founder photograph, and the brand's claim is specifically about real people in Charleston.

sections.purpose: Show the range of drinks by spirit, which is how the recipes are actually tagged.
sections.component: index list; one expandable row per spirit
sections.rationale: The brief says recipes are tagged by spirit and are the brand's SEO engine, so the index is organised by spirit rather than by mood or occasion.

sections.purpose: Give the flagship award-winner its own moment and note its different ratio.
sections.component: feature split; the Bloody Mary bottle beside its exception copy
sections.rationale: It is the one product with a different rule (4:1), and stating the exception plainly is more trustworthy than pretending every bottle behaves the same.

media.alt: Bloody Mary 1L bottle, smoked sea salt and chiles
media.rationale: The flagship bottle shot, matching the treatment used for the opening bottle so the range reads as one family.

sections.purpose: Cover the non-alcoholic use, which is a real product capability.
sections.component: feature split; finished mocktail photograph beside short copy
sections.rationale: Every mixer is non-alcoholic on its own, which doubles the audience; the brief states it explicitly, so it earns a section rather than an asterisk.

media.alt: Virgin Bloody Mary served over ice, made with the mixer and no spirit
media.rationale: A finished mocktail is the proof that the bottle works without alcohol.

sections.purpose: List the publications that have covered the brand.
sections.component: proof row; outlet names in a single horizontal band
sections.rationale: Editor coverage is the only third-party proof the brand actually has — there are no customer testimonials — so it is presented plainly as a list of names, with no invented quotes.

sections.purpose: Route trade buyers to the right distributor without changing the consumer voice.
sections.component: editorial column; distributors named in running copy
sections.rationale: Wholesale exists but the brief is explicit that it must not become the voice of the site, so it sits low on the page in the same plain register as everything else.

sections.purpose: Close on the price and a single call to action.
sections.rationale: The price is the strongest closing argument — one bottle at $12 replaces a shelf of ingredients — so it is stated rather than hidden behind the click.
Records the substituted display face and the contact route, so the licensing decision is visible rather than buried.

skipped_sections.reason: The brand has no customer quotes anywhere on the live site, and the operator explicitly forbade inventing any. Editor coverage exists and is used instead, as a plain list of outlet names in the press section — never rewritten into a quote.
The Instagram handle is verified but no posts were fetched, so there is no real image or caption to show. A social wall built from nothing would be fabricated content.
A single hat SKU exists but its price was never observed in the extracted markup, so a shop section for it would have to invent the price or omit the one fact a shopper needs.

decisions.decision: Open on the mix ratio rather than a lifestyle photograph.
alternatives_considered: Full-bleed lifestyle hero with the wordmark overlaid
Founders' story as the opening section
decisions.why_chosen: The ratio is the brand's shortest sentence and its actual promise. A lifestyle hero would look like every other beverage site and delay the one fact that removes the objection to making a cocktail at home.

decisions.decision: Organise the recipe section by spirit, not by occasion or mixer.
alternatives_considered: Grid of recipe cards with finished-drink photography
decisions.why_chosen: The brief states recipes are tagged by spirit and are the brand's SEO engine. Sorting by what the visitor already owns matches how someone actually decides what to drink.

decisions.decision: State the Bloody Mary's 4:1 exception in its own section instead of a footnote.
alternatives_considered: Omit it and keep one clean rule
decisions.why_chosen: Hiding the exception would make the headline rule wrong for the flagship product. Saying it plainly costs one section and buys trust.

decisions.decision: Use the price as the closing headline.
decisions.why_chosen: $12 for roughly eight drinks is the strongest argument the brand has, and the brief lists it as a published fact. Withholding it until checkout wastes it.

decisions.decision: No customer testimonials anywhere, despite the conversion value.
alternatives_considered: Paraphrase editor coverage into quote form
decisions.why_chosen: The brand has none, and the operator forbade inventing them. Editor coverage is listed as bare outlet names so nothing is attributed to anyone who did not say it.
